verdicts.correction: Upheld, with a header fix wanted before landing: the header credits the case-insensitive METHOD-name mapping to docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-64, but that row documents only the PROGRAM-name mapping (ProgramTable.NameEquals). The expectation still follows from the spec: under the COBOL convention (§8.3.2.2) the literal names the method-name as a COBOL word, and SayHi/sayhi/SAYHI are the same word. Cite that reasoning instead of DOC-A.1-64 for method-names.

Drop conformance:2014/l1c06_entry_convention_oo from GR-11.9.7.4-4 and leave the row a GAP (test-needed, vacuous while COBOL is the only convention, PB298). GR4 a) and b) say a no-clause class or interface INHERITS its convention from the first class or interface in its INHERITS clause. COBOL.NET has only one convention (DOC-A.1-64), so an implementation that ignored INHERITS and used c) (default COBOL) would print exactly BASE-HI/BASE-HI/DER-EXTRA/IF-PING/MAIN-END. Nothing tells a) or b) apart from c). The derivation also misattributes lines. (1) Per §8.3.2.2, a method invoked through a non-universal reference follows 'the entry convention of the class or interface that contains the method'. For INVOKE OD "SAYHI" that is SayHi's container L1C06JB, whose convention is the explicit COBOL, not an inherited one. (2) INVOKE OI "ping": Ping is declared in L1C06JIA (explicit COBOL) and implemented in L1C06JC (arm c)). L1C06JIB declares no method, so its inherited convention (arm b)) never governs any mapping. (3) MAIN-END does not depend on any entry convention, so it does not pin arm c) either. The program shows only that a no-clause class maps method-names in the COBOL way. That is a c)-or-a) result, not the INHERITS rule.
